page: Microsoft Azure D48as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing x86_64 architecture, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance is configured with 192 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio. It does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, operating as a stateless compute resource designed to interface with remote Premium Storage. Hardware execution extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, AES, and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the D48as_v6 demonstrates top-quartile compute capability. Multi-core evaluations in stress-ng and Geekbench register within the top 25% of tested systems, driven by strong core scaling and high instruction throughput. PassMark CPU tests yield 63,028.71 points, reinforced by strong results in software compilation and multi-threaded decompression tasks. Cache memory bandwidth reaches 3,648.65 GB/sec, facilitating rapid data access within CPU caches, though uncached large-block memory read and write speeds settle into average benchmark percentiles.

The hardware configuration yields high transaction rates for memory-bound tasks, delivering 66.46 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database scores. While small language models achieve high text generation speeds on the CPU, larger model inference performance degrades due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. With zero local disk, IO-intensive applications depend entirely on networked storage throughput. The D48as_v6 is well suited for enterprise application backends, distributed build environments, in-memory caching systems, and relational databases.
description: Microsoft Azure D48as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores at 3.7 GHz, paired with 192 GB of memory in a standard 4:1 memory-to-core ratio. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware acceleration flags, while omitting local storage and GPU accelerators, functioning instead as a stateless compute node dependent on remote storage. Benchmark results place the system in the top quartile for multi-core stress tests, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU metrics. It demonstrates high efficiency in in-memory tasks, achieving 66.46 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside rapid software compilation and multi-threaded decompression. However, uncached memory bandwidth remains average, and absence of dedicated accelerators limits large model machine learning execution. The instance offers a balanced resource profile for multi-threaded enterprise services, in-memory caching, backend API clusters, and high-volume relational databases.
